clue.text: Broadcast shows monarch's head in carriage

indicators.note: the monarch's initial goes in the middle of the word for carriage

parts.note: transit is the carrying or conveying of goods or people, so carriage

indicators.note: a monarch's head is the first letter of the word monarch

explanation.surface: A news broadcast shows the king or queen arriving in a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast a programme is to send it out over the airwaves, a synonym.

clue.text: Avoid team on stage

indicators.note: in a down clue, the team's word sits on top of the stage's word

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A team walks onto a theatre stage, or perhaps avoids it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to dodge it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Demand protection

definitions.meaning: to ask a price or demand payment
a person in your ... is under your care and protection

explanation.surface: Like a racketeer asking for protection money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses: one asks a price, the other means custody or care.

clue.text: Earth perhaps flat? Thinking, originally

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface; plane also means level

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of Thinking

explanation.surface: Asks whether people once thought the Earth was flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals that the Earth is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one example of a world orbiting the Sun, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: The cost of a round?

parts.note: a round sounds like drinks bought in a pub, but it is a round of golf and the fee paid to play the course

explanation.surface: Someone asks what buying a round of drinks will cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf clubs charge visitors a fixed sum to play their course; that payment is this fee.

clue.text: Feel sorry about Garbo, briefly

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: briefly means the name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Greta Garbo was the Swedish-born Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: Someone feels sorry for the reclusive film star Greta Garbo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks part of the definition but supplies RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret something is to feel sorry or remorseful about it, a synonym.

clue.text: Stuff and nonsense in little black book I found during storm

indicators.note: these letters are found in the middle of the word for storm

parts.note: to storm or rush is to charge forward violently
B is the short form of black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the contents of a little black book found during a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is an exclamation of scorn, the same as saying stuff and nonsense.

clue.text: Bear, Rupert, initially appearing in annual?

indicators.note: the initial appears inside the word for annual

parts.note: an annual is a yearly book, like the Rupert annuals for children

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Rupert

explanation.surface: Asks whether Rupert Bear will appear in this year's children's annual.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Bear is a British children's comic-strip character with a yearly annual. 'Bear' is the verb here: to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate or put up with it, as in 'brook no argument'.

clue.text: Bit of energy in éclair: unusually, about zero!

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, that is around, the zero
unusually means the letters of the pastry word are arranged out of their normal order

parts.note: O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A dieter is pleased that an éclair has, unusually, almost no energy content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges ECLAIR to CALRIE, which goes 'about' O.
explanation.definitionFit: A calorie is a small unit of food energy, so a bit of energy.

clue.text: Monster ride, mostly round perimeter of parks

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: to cycle is to ride a bicycle
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the perimeter of a word is its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes a monster cycle ride round the edge of the parks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was a one-eyed giant, a classic monster of Homer's Odyssey.

clue.text: Snare elk — name for male

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: the European elk is the same animal North Americans call a moose

explanation.surface: A hunter's instruction: trap the elk and record the name of the male.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope that tightens, used as a snare to trap animals.

clue.text: Grass, admitting swindle, comes to regret about being a teller of tales

indicators.note: comes to means the turned word is added on
admitting means the word for grass lets the swindle in

parts.note: to grass or rat is to inform on someone
a con is a swindle

indicators.note: about means the word for regret is turned around

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: An informer who admits a swindle comes to regret being a storyteller.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone skilled at telling anecdotes and stories, a synonym.

clue.text: To enjoy what's available, use a certain something as best you can

definitions.meaning: the idiom means to get full benefit from the circumstances you have

definitions.text: use a certain something as best you can
definitions.meaning: read literally, it means exploit a particular thing, the pronoun standing for something

explanation.surface: Advice to enjoy what you have and use it as well as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means exploiting an opportunity fully; read literally, 'it' is the certain something.

clue.text: Kit Carson, say, in theatre role upon retirement

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: An actor takes the role of Kit Carson in a theatre on retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: Kit Carson was an American frontiersman who trapped furs; 'say' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Carson worked catching beavers for fur in the American West, an example of the occupation.

clue.text: British love meat, visiting Alabama, more than anything else

indicators.note: visiting means these letters go inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama
love is zero in tennis, written O
veal is meat from a calf

explanation.surface: British visitors to Alabama love the meat above all.
explanation.definitionFit: Above all is an idiom meaning most importantly, more than anything else.

clue.text: Old soldier, or cadet in need of training

indicators.note: something needing training is not yet in shape, so the letters must be reworked

explanation.surface: An old soldier, or a young cadet, who needs drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: British soldiers of earlier centuries wore scarlet tunics and were nicknamed for them.

clue.text: Figure on horseback to move forward

parts.note: a figure is a shape or outline
a jockey who is up is riding the horse

explanation.surface: A figure on horseback urges the horse forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape up is to develop or progress, so to move forward.

clue.text: Recommend Edinburgh lawyer?

definitions.meaning: to speak in favour of or recommend
in Scotland a barrister is called by this title, so an Edinburgh courtroom lawyer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to recommend a lawyer in Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to back publicly; the noun is the Scottish term for a barrister.

clue.text: Nag, pinto, prepared for moving

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are made ready in a new form

explanation.surface: A nag and a pinto horse are made ready for transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like relocating the horses, but it means emotionally touching.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poignant is emotionally touching, which is one sense of moving.

clue.text: Renowned painter ordered vindaloo and rice

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A famous painter orders a curry and rice at an Indian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' pretends to be what he did at the restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian Renaissance artist of the Mona Lisa is among the most famous of painters.

clue.text: Record crowd causing standstill

parts.note: a log is a written record
a jam is a crowd packed tightly

explanation.surface: A record crowd brings traffic to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a blockage or deadlock where nothing moves, so a standstill.

clue.text: To that extent, carrier is off course

parts.note: as means to that extent, as in 'as far as'
a tray is used to carry things

explanation.surface: An aircraft carrier has drifted so far it is off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means away from the correct path, so off course.

clue.text: District Attorney: I vet awkward case

parts.note: DA is the American abbreviation for District Attorney

indicators.note: awkward means the letters are arranged clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: A prosecutor says they will vet an awkward legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is a grammatical case, not a legal one.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar this is the case for an indirect object, as in Latin and German.

clue.text: New First Lady? Republican? Surely not!

parts.note: in the Bible Eve was the first woman

explanation.surface: Reacting with disbelief to news of a Republican First Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Never! is an exclamation of disbelief, the same as saying surely not.

clue.text: What a soldier may be seen wearing in much admired film

definitions.text: What a soldier may be seen wearing

parts.note: great means outstanding and much admired
a film is a thin layer or coat

explanation.surface: A soldier character appears in a much-admired war film.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy overcoat issued to soldiers, so typically worn by one.

clue.text: Fellow associated with northern group of witches

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a fellow or chap

explanation.surface: A man linked to a northern group of witches.
explanation.definitionFit: A coven is a gathering of witches, traditionally thirteen, the collective noun.

clue.text: Finally consuming last of cheese, if nothing else

indicators.note: consuming means the phrase for finally swallows the letter

parts.note: at last means finally

indicators.note: the last of cheese is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone finally eats the last of the cheese, if nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: At least is used to mean if nothing else or anyway, an idiomatic match.

clue.text: Long-serving animal expert near ground

parts.note: a vet treats animals

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A long-serving animal expert stands near the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran has served a long time; used as an adjective it means long-serving.
